frozen_claim.title: Colorado named-entity/jurisdiction frame with narrow other-jurisdiction administrative suppression
frozen_claim.lede: The neuron is primarily a Colorado named-entity and jurisdiction detector. Strong positives occur on explicit Colorado or Colorado-derived names, Colorado institutions/places, C.R.S. citations, Colorado area codes/URLs/local media, and Colorado statehood/history or higher-education/science frames, often on a nearby space or function word in the causal prefix. The negative pole is much narrower than earlier: broad non-Colorado place-name and measurement rules were withdrawn because many such contexts are positive or weak. Reliable negatives are other-jurisdiction administrative/contact/citation strings; negative coverage is sparse.
frozen_claim.what_would_change_my_mind: I would restore a non-Colorado place-name negative rule if many non-Colorado place contexts, including Bolivia, Nepal, Texas, Utah, and New Mexico, were consistently strongly negative rather than positive or weak. I would withdraw Colorado specificity if explicit Colorado names in the causal prefix were often weak or negative without an intervening factor. I would revise the administrative-negative rules if 701/775/435, N.D.C.C., or Qinghai grant strings were often strong positive. I would add a new positive rule if strong non-Colorado positives clustered around a nameable recurring expression; currently they remain unresolved. Tiny near-zero sign flips alone should not overturn the supported patterns.
frozen_claim.one_paragraph: Positive when the prefix before the marked position contains 'Colorado' or a Colorado-built name ('state of Colorado', 'University of Colorado', 'Colorado State University', 'Colorado School of Public Health', 'Colorado Department of ...', 'Colorado Women's Education Foundation', 'Colorado Labor Wars') or a Colorado-linked place/institution ('Denver', 'Boulder', 'Arvada', 'Longmont', 'Aspen', 'Pueblo', 'Rocky Mountain' in a Colorado frame). The high value may sit on an adjacent space or function word inside that name. The cue must be in the causal prefix; continuation after the anchor (e.g. 'Colorado Plateaus' after 'within') does not count. Non-Colorado names do not by themselves establish a negative response. Positive on the Colorado statutory citation pattern '§ 22-5-119, C.R.S.', '22-5-199, C.R.S.' or 'per statutory reference in [number]' within Colorado blended-learning or state-law material. High values can fall on spaces, digits, section symbols, hyphens, or punctuation inside or immediately before the citation. The same punctuation and digits without the Colorado statute frame do not suffice; N.D.C.C. or Qinghai grant numbers are not positive by format alone. Positive when a Colorado entity/address/local-media frame is present: Denver 303/720/970 numbers such as 720-848-18..., 'Longmont, CO', '.co.us', 'colostate.edu', or '9NEWS'. The high value may be on the space, slash, digit, or adjacent ordinary token. Area code, phone punctuation, or URL form alone is not a cue; analogous 701/775/435 strings in other-jurisdiction administrative material are not positive. Positive in Colorado state-history frames: 'Colorado became the thirty-eighth state', 'Its nickname is the Centennial State', 'Colorado became a state on August 1, 1876', and 'Colorado Labor Wars, 1903-1904'. The response can land on 'is' before the nickname or a space before the date. Parallel statehood or history facts for other states are not enough; they are not negative by topic alone. Positive around Colorado-linked universities, research, and local news: CU Boulder, University of Colorado, Colorado State University, Colorado School of Public Health, Denver Museum of Nature & Science, NOAA/NCAR in Boulder, CSU Extension, and 9NEWS. High values can appear on 'University', 'State', 'Public', 'Atmospheric', 'Boulder', 'Denver', or nearby spaces/digits only within such a frame. The bare generic word outside a Colorado frame is not reliable.
frozen_claim.negative_pole: Negative on contact, citation, or grant strings tied to another jurisdiction in the prefix: North Dakota '(701) 328-1504' or a 701 phone in Game and Fish CWD material, N.D.C.C. '§ 28-33-02' with hyphens and digits, Nevada/Utah 775/435 phone strings, or Qinghai grant 'No. 11761056' with parentheses and digits. The cue is the other-jurisdiction administrative/identifier frame, often involving punctuation and digits; generic numbers, punctuation, or a non-Colorado place name alone are not reliable negatives. Negative on legal or administrative boilerplate for another jurisdiction: North Dakota Department of Agriculture/IPM address-phone block, North Dakota Game and Fish CWD contact, N.D.C.C. citations, and New Mexico or Qinghai grant/address material. Purely generic legal prose without a jurisdiction cue is weak or near zero. This rule does not suppress ordinary discussion of other states or regions, which can be positive or weak; it targets formatted other-jurisdiction administrative and legal identifiers.
